correctness.rationale: The alternant quotient is e₂ at the five distinct complex nodes. Reduction in the basis 1,ω,…,ω^(N/2−1) pairs the ten products with their negatives, preserving multiplicity. If an antipodal node pair u,−u is present, its cross terms cancel and the four residual terms force another antipodal pair v,−v with v²=−u². In the other case opposite edge products come from disjoint edges. Each of the five vertices is omitted by one of the five edge matchings, so reducing each product relation modulo two forces equal parity of all five exponents. Dividing the shifted exponents by two descends to N/2 with five distinct nodes; a quartet at that order lifts to a quartet, and orders at most four are impossible. A quartet annuls both e₁ and e₂, proving sufficiency. The {0,1,2,4} minor on u,−u,iu and the outsider v is a nonzero Vandermonde times iu+v, so the singular rank is exactly four. Disjoint cosets give the claimed count without double counting. I inspected verify_dyadic_5minor.py and verification_output.txt: the reported exhaustive integer tests at 8,16,32 and four determinant evaluations corroborate the argument; I did not execute the frozen script and the proof is not predicated on these tests.
